# QA Plan: Sprint 8 — Re-verdict and Advance the Stage

**Date**: 2026-08-26
**Generated by**: `/qa-plan sprint`
**Scope**: 19 stories across 9 systems
**Engine**: Redot 26.2 (Godot 4.x-compatible) — `./redot`
**Sprint File**: `production/sprints/sprint-8.md`
**Suite at time of writing**: **1307 / 1307, 0 orphans**

---

## ⚠ Read this first — what kind of plan this is

**This plan is retroactive for 14 of its 19 stories, and that is a defect in the process, not a
feature of the plan.** Sprint 8 was written as a *validation* sprint with no implementation work,
so no QA plan was thought necessary. Nine implementation stories then landed anyway (S8-10…S8-18),
and the sprint reached ~1,300 passing tests without anyone ever writing down what "tested" was
supposed to mean.

★ **The suite is green and the work is genuinely well-tested** — this is not a plan that discovered
rotten work. It is a plan whose value is almost entirely in **the two gaps below**, both of which
were found by doing the one thing a QA plan does: reading the acceptance criteria and asking what
actually verifies them.

⛔ **Sprints 6 and 7 have no QA plan either.** This is the third sprint in a row without one.

## ⛔⛔ FINDING 1 — The GDD acceptance criteria contradict the shipped game

**Severity: BLOCKING for S8-02/S8-03.** This is the finding of this plan.

`base-production.md`'s **Acceptance Criteria** section — the exact text a QA tester is told to
verify against, and which opens *"Each criterion is independently verifiable by a QA tester without
reading this GDD"* — still describes the pre-S8-13 game:

| GDD Acceptance Criteria says | Shipped code + test says | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| HQ produces **`{Scout}`** | HQ produces **`{Builder}`**, exactly 1 type | ⛔ **STALE** |
| **Production Outpost** | renamed **Barracks** | ⛔ **STALE** |
| Production Outpost produces `{Trooper, Heavy, Sniper}` | Barracks produces **4** types — Scout moved here | ⛔ **STALE** |
| Production Outpost **cost 9** | Barracks `build_cost` **600** | ⛔ **STALE** |
| Economy Outpost **cost 4, time 1** | **cost 1000, time 3, upkeep 200** | ⛔ **STALE** (since S6-09) |
| *(no Builder anywhere)* | Builder: hp 3, attack 0, `attack_range` 0, `produce_cost` 150, `can_build` true | ⛔ **ABSENT** |

`unit-system.md`'s Acceptance Criteria section names **four** unit types and asserts *"each unit
type is instantiated… they match the table exactly"*. **There are five.** The Builder appears in
that section **zero** times — including the `base_defense` assertion that claims to cover "all four
types (Scout / Trooper / Heavy / Sniper)".

### ★★ Why this matters more than a documentation nit

**The GDD body WAS updated.** `base-production.md` line 329 carries the full S8-13 decision — *"Build
belongs to a BUILDER, and the Builder is spent"* — written out properly with its three consequences.
**Only the Acceptance Criteria section was left behind.**

⇒ **The part of the GDD that describes the design is current. The part that says how to verify it is
a year out of date in game-time.** A QA tester following this GDD to the letter would file the
shipped, correct, deliberately-designed game as a defect.

⚠ **This is the S8-11 pattern for the third time.** That story's own finding was *"the pass ran
BACKWARDS — the decision moved in the UX spec and the code, and the GDD was the laggard."* Same
shape here, one level deeper: the decision moved into the GDD **prose** and the GDD's **own
acceptance criteria** were the laggard.

### Required action — before S8-02 analyses anything

- [ ] `base-production.md` — update the template Acceptance Criteria to the shipped values
      (HQ `{Builder}`; Barracks name, cost 600, 4 producible types; Economy Outpost 1000/3/200)
- [ ] `base-production.md` — add acceptance criteria for the **Builder consumption rule**: the
      Builder is destroyed *after* the structure is placed, and its destruction events are
      **appended, not discarded**. ★ Both are load-bearing invariants with tests but no stated AC.
- [ ] `unit-system.md` — extend the type table and the `base_defense` criterion to **five** types
- [ ] Re-run `/consistency-check` afterwards — ⚠ the entity registry may carry the same stale stats

## ✅ FINDING 3 — The accent gate did not cover the Builder, and the Builder failed it

**Severity: was BLOCKING. ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-26 (S8-19) — art repainted, gate now enumerates.**
Found by capturing Finding 2's evidence, which is the whole argument for capturing it.

Measured with the gate's own formula (α ≥ 40/255, v ≥ 60/255, s ≥ 0.45):

| Archetype | rush | boom | neutral |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Scout | 45.6% | 45.3% | 0.0% |
| Trooper | 42.5% | 42.6% | 0.0% |
| Heavy | 62.7% | 62.0% | 0.0% |
| Sniper | 43.2% | 43.7% | 0.5% |
| ⛔ **Builder — was** | **22.8%** | **22.9%** | 0.1% |
| ✅ **Builder — now** | **33.9%** | **34.2%** | 0.1% |

`accent_coverage_test.gd` asserts an owned-faction floor of **30.0%** and a roster spread ceiling of
**2.5×**. The Builder is **7.2 points under the floor**, and including it takes the spread to
**62.7 / 22.8 = 2.75×**. ⇒ **It would fail two of the suite's four assertions.**

⛔ **It does not fail, because line 21 keeps a hand-written list:**
```gdscript
const _ARCHETYPES: Array[String] = ["scout", "trooper", "heavy", "sniper"]
```

### ★★ This is S8-14's finding, in the sibling test, still live

S8-14's entire lesson was: *"Both guards carried a hand-written list of the nine types, so they
guarded only what somebody had remembered to transcribe… A coverage check that keeps its own copy of
the thing it covers is not a coverage check."* It rewrote `test_every_vs_type_now_has_shipped_art`
and its glow-mask sibling to enumerate `UnitTypes.ALL`.

⚠ **`accent_coverage_test.gd` was written earlier (S8-05), for the same purpose, and was not
touched.** So the gate created because *"the Sniper defect shipped and survived a full art sprint
because nothing measured it, and every wave-2 unit has the same failure mode available"* — **does
not measure the roster's newest unit.** The next unit added will not be measured either.

★★ **The lesson generalises past both instances: fixing an anti-pattern where you found it is not
fixing it.** Sprint 8 has now found three lists-that-should-have-been-enumerations and fixed two.

### ✅ How it was resolved — the art, not the threshold

**User's call, 2026-08-26: repaint to clear 30%.** The test's own failure message prescribes the
route — *"Fix the ART, not this threshold: raise saturated coverage via `promote_accent.py` and
re-derive. Do NOT touch the silhouette."*

`promote_accent.py --target 34` **grows the existing accent regions outward** instead of inventing
new ones: the artist already decided *where* the accent belongs and dilation only decides how far it
extends, so the result reads as a bolder version of the same design. ⚠ Two earlier approaches
recorded in that tool — brightest-N pixels and value-banded components — both **measured correct and
looked wrong** (orange speckle; a corduroy artefact). **Silhouette untouched.**

★★ **34 was chosen by eye from rendered candidates, not as the smallest passing number:**

| Candidate | Shipped | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|
| was | 22.8% | ⛔ fails the floor |
| ✅ **34** | **33.9%** | Clears by ~4 pts · grey upper hull still dominates · **still the roster's least-coloured unit by 8.6 pts** |
| 38 | 38.1% | Passes; grey mass visibly shrinking |
| 42 | 42.7% | ⛔ reads as a combat unit, level with the Trooper's 42.5% |

⚠ **Why not the minimum that passes:** the brief deliberately wants the Builder greyest — *"the
silhouette has to say 'not a soldier' before any colour is read"*. But ownership must still read on
a busy board. **33.9% is the point where both are true**, and it was picked by compositing all four
at shipped scale on the stage colour — per the standing rule that *a correct metric with wrong art
is the normal case; if a number is the only check, bad art passes.*

✅ **Gate now enumerates `UnitTypes.ALL`** through `EntitySpriteCatalog.type_token` — the same call
the renderer uses to build a sprite path, so the gate cannot drift from what the game loads.
✅ **Verified to have teeth**, per the project's distrust-clean-results rule: raising the floor to
40% fails naming *"builder rush … 33.9% … below the 40.0% floor"* and *"builder boom … 34.2%"*.
✅ Roster spread **2.75× → 1.85×**. Suite **1307/1307**.

## Automated Tests — the one that changed how this project tests

### S8-17 — AI opponent · Integration
**Test file**: `tests/integration/ai-opponent/ai_plays_a_real_opening_test.gd`
**Covers**: `ai-opponent.md` AC-22 (cancel-build scoring), and a gap no AC states.

★★ **This test is the sprint's most important QA artefact and the pattern to copy.** Every prior AI
test **scored one candidate or drove one turn**, and all 38 of `ai-opponent.md`'s acceptance
criteria are written that way — GIVEN a board state, THEN this score. An AI that produced a Builder,
spent it on a Barracks, **cancelled the Barracks for the refund**, and repeated that every turn
until it owned nothing but its HQ with 6,000+ Credits banked **satisfies every one of them.**

The new test asserts **outcomes over six real turns**: the AI commits actions, **still owns a
structure at the end of a turn**, fields an army, and spends rather than hoards. Verified failing
without the fix.

⛔⛔ **AND THE UNIT TESTS WERE PART OF THE BUG.** `_cancel_build_value` returned raw Credits where
AC-22 specifies `CANCEL_REFUND_RATE × build_cost × CREDIT_TO_AP_RATE`. **The tests asserted the
implementation**, so code and tests agreed with each other while both contradicted the GDD — a
defect a test written from the code **cannot catch by construction.**

> ### ★★ The rule to carry into Sprint 9
> **A test whose expected value is read from the thing under test proves only that the code equals
> itself.** Sprint 8 found this twice:
> 1. **S8-17** — AI tests asserting the implementation instead of AC-22's formula.
> 2. **S8-14** — art-coverage guards that kept a *hand-transcribed list* of the nine unit types, so
>    the Builder shipped as a magenta placeholder and the suite stayed green.
>    ★ *A coverage check that keeps its own copy of the thing it covers is not a coverage check.*
>
> ### ⚠ A suspected third instance, investigated and CLEARED — recorded because the check is
> ### the same one that found the other two, and it is worth knowing how to tell them apart
> `build_verb_legal_build_tiles_occupancy_test.gd:529` and `cancel_build_refund_test.gd` assert
> against **`StructureTypes.BARRACKS.build_cost`** — the data file itself — which has the exact
> shape of the anti-pattern above. **It is not one, and changing it would make both tests worse.**
>
> ★ **The derivation is deliberate and documented in the code:**
> > *"S6-09: derived from the type, not hardcoded. This test is about the ABSENCE of an economy-tech
> > discount hook; pinning the literal cost made it fail when the Factory was re-statted, which is
> > unrelated churn."*
> > *"S6-02: derived, not restated — the ×100 rescale moved build_cost 9 → 900."*
>
> ★★ **The distinction that matters:** `test_effective_build_cost_equals_base_exactly_under_neutral`
> asserts an **identity** — *effective cost equals base when no modifier applies*. A literal there
> would assert the wrong thing: it would pass for the wrong reason if a discount hook were added
> **and** the base changed to compensate. **Derivation is the correct assertion for a relationship;
> a literal is the correct assertion for a value.**
>
> ✅ **And the values ARE pinned** — `structure_schema_templates_config_test.gd` carries every
> literal (Barracks 600/2, Economy Outpost 1000/3, Defensive 500/2, Lab 800/2, HQ hp 40, and
> `{Builder}` explicitly). ⚠ **Know that this is the one load-bearing test in the group**: every
> derived assertion in base-production leans on it, so it is the file to be most careful with.
>
> ⇒ **The test to distrust is the one that derives a VALUE it claims to verify** (S8-17's
> `_cancel_build_value`, S8-14's transcribed type list), **not one that derives a value it is using
> to check a RELATIONSHIP.** Both look identical at a glance; only the assertion's subject differs.

### S8-12 — Command/Action interface · Integration
**Test files**: `tests/integration/command-action-interface/keyboard_only_flow_test.gd`,
`tests/integration/vertical-slice/build_picker_wiring_test.gd`
**Covers**: `command-action-interface.md` **AC-9** — *"complete a full move using only the keyboard"*.

⛔ **AC-9 had no test at all until this sprint**, and the behaviour it describes was **completely
broken**: Godot's `Button` does not accept the press half of a keyboard activation, so the press
also reached `_unhandled_input`, re-selected the entity, and **rebuilt the menu out from under the
row that was mid-press**.

⚠ **The bug was invisible unless the cursor stood on a selectable owned entity — which is the normal
case**, because selecting one is how the menu opens. On an empty tile it worked. *Same keypress,
opposite outcome*, which is exactly how it was reported.

★ **These tests push real `InputEventKey` through the viewport and press real picker rows**, because
**every method in both chains already worked when called by hand.** That is the only reason they
catch anything — and it is why `build_type_chosen` being emitted into a void survived so long
(**the third dead hook found this way**, after `board_cursor_cycle` and `notify_action_applied`).

**Recommended, not yet done**: a standing check that every declared signal has at least one
production listener. Three dead hooks is a pattern, not bad luck.

### S8-13 · Logic + Integration — the acceptance criteria that need writing
Existing tests are good (including one **inverted** rule — *"a friendly structure alone no longer
makes a build tile"* — the rule most likely to be reintroduced by accident). ⛔ **What is missing is
upstream**: see Finding 1. Two invariants are tested but have **no stated AC**:
- the Builder is destroyed **after** the structure is placed (so a mid-apply failure cannot leave a
  player who has paid with no Builder *and* no building)
- its destruction events are **appended, not discarded** (else the sprite stands beside the building
  it became and the population counter never learns)

### S8-05 / S8-06 / S8-07 · already gated
No further automation required. ⚠ **S8-07's 1.15 scale is reasoned, not observed — no Deck has run
this build.** ★ Note the sprint's own warning attached to it: a first measurement of this was
**wrong in a way that agreed with expectations**, and was caught only by re-introducing the
"failing" value and finding it did not fail.

**Who signs off**: user, then qa-lead writes findings back into the S5-03 / S5-04 reports
**Evidence**: prose answers in `production/playtests/SESSION-2026-08-26-play-and-answer.md`

- [ ] **Rebuild the binary first** — ⛔ it predates S8-12…S8-17
      `./redot --headless --export-release "Linux Release" "$PWD/builds/linux/Overclock.x86_64"`
- [ ] Close any stale instance — `pgrep -f Overclock.x86_64`
- [ ] Q1–Q3 (naive observer) — ★ skippable, record "no observer available"
- [ ] **A** — does the swing feel alive?
- [ ] **C** — does tempo read at a glance?
- [ ] **D** — ★★ does spending Credits feel like a **tempo cost**?

> ⛔⛔ **D's subject matter changed this sprint and the question did not.** Build is the economic
> action whose *feel* D asks about, and **it now costs a whole Builder unit rather than a HUD
> click** (S8-13). ★ That is arguably *closer* to what D was always asking — but it means **no
> earlier session's answer transfers**, and the answer given must be about this build.
>
> ⚠ **D is subjective language and the standards require a benchmark alongside it.** The benchmark
> here is the counterfactual: *would you rather have kept the Builder?* If that question never
> occurred to the player during the game, D has failed regardless of what they say afterwards.

### S8-06 — Controller glyphs

## Smoke Test Scope

Run via `/smoke-check sprint` before any QA hand-off:

1. Game launches to main menu without crash — **and the exported binary does too**, not just `./redot`
2. New Skirmish starts
3. ★ **HQ → Builder → walk → Barracks → army**, the sprint's changed critical path. The Builder must
   be **gone** afterwards and the population counter must agree
4. ⛔ **Complete one full command using only the keyboard** — this was broken all sprint (S8-12)
5. ⛔ **Play six turns against the AI and confirm it still owns structures at the end** — this was
   broken all sprint (S8-17)
6. Build picker opens **and commits** — the path that was wired to nothing
7. No new frame spikes; board renders correctly at **1280×800**
8. Save/load round-trip, if the save system is in the slice

★ Items 3–6 are all new this sprint and **all four were broken at some point during it.**

### ★ Carried to Sprint 9 — process, not content
- **Write the QA plan before the sprint, not after.** Three sprints running have skipped it.
- **Declare `Type:` on every story.** All 19 classifications here are inferred.
- **Never assert an expected value by reading the thing under test** — when the value *is* what you
  are verifying. Found twice this sprint (S8-17, S8-14). ⚠ A third suspected case was investigated
  and **cleared**: deriving a value to check a *relationship* is correct, and "fixing" it would have
  broken two good tests. ★ **The subject of the assertion is what separates them.**
- **A standing dead-signal check.** Three dead hooks found by accident is a pattern.
